LDES10-UNORD-001.rationale: Multiple modes are optional extension capability metadata and do not affect a baseline conformance claim.

LDES10-UNORD-003.rationale: Modes beyond unordered and ordered ascending are explicitly extension space.

LDES10-UNORD-016.rationale: Source selection is an optional dereferencing extension outside the common adapter contract.

LDES10-UNORD-033.rationale: External JSON-LD context cache observation needs a controlled document-loader hook in addition to the existing origin request log.

LDES10-UNORD-045.rationale: Authorization handling is optional and requires credential provisioning that is intentionally outside the public baseline suite.

LDES10-UNORD-048.rationale: The current process protocol collects events after adapter completion and therefore cannot reliably measure immediate streaming latency.

LDES10-ORD-002.rationale: Inferring immutability from relation bounds is an optional optimization.

LDES10-ORD-003.rationale: Timestamp or sequence bookmarks are an optional state strategy; restart behavior is tested without requiring an implementation technique.

LDES10-EXTRACT-001.rationale: TREE-profile extraction is an optional named capability and needs a profile capability flag before it can be selected fairly.

LDES10-EXTRACT-009.rationale: Named-graph upsert interpretation is optional consumer behavior; named-graph dataset extraction itself is tested.

LDES10-PIPE-001.rationale: This constrains a downstream consumer pipeline, not the traversal client; run-finalization signaling is tested separately.

LDES10-CTX-010.rationale: Chronological interpretation is scored in ordered traversal; this row also applies to broader consumers.

LDES10-CTX-011.rationale: Executing SHACL validation is processor behavior; the client suite verifies shape context communication.

LDES10-CTX-012.rationale: Logical-AND shape validation is processor behavior; the context fixture discriminates communication of multiple shapes.

LDES10-CTX-013.rationale: Selecting latest versions is consumer behavior; versionTimestampPath extraction is tested.

LDES10-CTX-014.rationale: Selecting latest versions is consumer behavior; versionSequencePath extraction is tested.

LDES10-CTX-015.rationale: Recovering prior update or deletion payloads requires a materializing consumer, beyond traversal and context extraction.

LDES10-RET-001.rationale: Completeness assumptions are consumer interpretation; absence and presence are exposed by the context event.

LDES10-RET-002.rationale: Availability assumptions outside a policy are consumer interpretation; policy discovery is tested.

LDES10-RET-006.rationale: Clock-skew calculation is retention-aware consumer behavior and needs a separate virtual-clock interpretation profile.

LDES10-RET-007.rationale: Duration evaluation against version timestamps is consumer behavior; path extraction is tested.

LDES10-RET-008.rationale: Historical policy interpretation is a separate retention-aware consumer profile, not baseline traversal.
